@SinkKole @AmandaAskell Reasonably solveable, in fact. We call it "democracy", and we try to *decentralize* power.

The idea is to try to not let this get destroyed by encouraging the monopoly of control over powerful tech into a small number of hands.
@SinkKole @AmandaAskell There is no amount of abundance to solve the problem that *power* is fundamentally *always* constrained.
@AmandaAskell Possibly you haven't spent enough time around power-seeking humans to viscerally understand this (in which case - lucky you!) but the evidence throughout history is nonetheless clear.

@AmandaAskell "if there's abundance despite that, the downsides of redistribution are likely to be very low and the benefits very high" is definitely *not* how power-seeking humans have *ever* behaved.

@AmandaAskell "the value of labor going to zero" is not a correct premise for the creation of a permanent underclass. There are many existence proofs of that, historically.

I've never seen anyone claim for such a premise before. What's the basis of it?

@AmandaAskell A large percentage of humans have spent a large percentage of the last few thousands years in this state - so rejecting it as something you don't "believe in" as a reasonably likely outcome needs strong support, IMO.
